bottleneck: Duchenne muscular dystrophy needs full-length dystrophin, a 14 kb transcript that no AAV can carry. Micro-dystrophin constructs fit but are truncated substitutes with uncertain long-term function, and systemic delivery to all muscles — including heart and diaphragm — at effective doses triggers liver toxicity and immune responses. Treating every muscle in the body from one infusion is a dosing paradox: enough vector for muscles means too much for the liver, and the heart's continuous workload may outpace what truncated protein can support.
current_state: Micro-dystrophin gene therapies are approved or in trials, but functional gains are modest and durability debated. Full-gene replacement has no delivery vehicle, and dual-vector approaches reconstitute poorly.

sources.title: Addressing the Limitations of AAV Vectors through Evolutionary Guided Vector Design

title: Duchenne's full dystrophin gene exceeds every vector
why_it_blocks: The most common fatal childhood genetic disease has a known fix that physically does not fit in the delivery vehicle. The payload limit is the disease's death sentence, and workarounds deliver only partial proteins with partial benefit.
